sections.title: App modernisation
sections.subtitle: Modernise legacy applications for safer releases, easier integration and scalable operations.

sections.heading: Modernise critical applications with business continuity in mind
sections.body:
When ageing applications constrain change, start with their business role, dependencies and operating risks. We assess what to retain, rehost, replatform, refactor or rebuild, then agree a staged roadmap rather than assume microservices are always the answer.

Baseline release lead time, incident rate and cost-to-change; use those measures to evaluate each wave. [Discuss your modernisation priorities](#get-in-touch).

sections.heading: From application estate to assured releases

items.description: Assess — Map dependencies, user journeys and operating risks. Client application owners confirm business priorities, access and baseline measures; agree the assessment and roadmap.
Design — Agree target architecture, migration waves, data controls and coexistence. The client approves acceptance criteria, rollback triggers and security requirements before build.
Build — Engineer UX, APIs and automated pipelines. Prototype priority screens and test them with representative users; review code, configuration and access changes.

Validate and hand over — Test migration, security and regression against the agreed gates. Record the release decision, rehearse rollback and transfer runbooks, monitoring and ownership to operations.

sections.heading: Evidence for each migration wave
sections.body:
A release decision should include dependency updates, regression results, security findings and rollback evidence—not just a completed build. Business owners accept priority journeys; technical owners record unresolved risks and operating readiness.

Compare release lead time, incidents and cost-to-change with the agreed baseline after each wave. Agree measurement periods and responsibility for the service after handover.

See [Our approach and commercial models](/company/our-approach) for delivery governance and engagement details.

sections.heading: Plan the right engagement
sections.description: Use Fixed Price for an agreed migration wave, or Time & Materials for estate discovery and evolving scope. A Dedicated Team supports sustained product engineering; Managed Service covers an agreed application operating scope. Outcome-Based work requires an evidenced baseline and agreed attribution.

items.title: What is needed for an estate assessment?
items.description: Application and dependency inventories, business-critical journeys, current architecture, incident history and change constraints. We agree access and confidentiality before reviewing sensitive material.

items.title: Can old and new applications coexist?
items.description: Yes, where the architecture supports it. Define interface and data ownership, reconciliation, migration waves and rollback triggers; validate the coexistence plan before cutover.

items.title: How do we choose refactoring or rebuilding?
items.description: Compare business fit, supportability, dependency risk and cost-to-change. Retaining or replatforming a suitable application can be preferable to rebuilding it.

items.title: Who owns the application after delivery?
items.description: Agree application, platform and support responsibilities before build. Handover includes configuration, release procedures, runbooks, monitoring and an accepted risk record.

items.title: What should we bring to the conversation?
items.description: Share the application estate, current constraints and target outcomes. We can then agree discovery scope, confidentiality requirements and a suitable delivery approach.
